title: Ten Martini for every periodic planar lattice
credit: Extends Avila–Jitomirskaya (Ten Martini, Annals 2009) and Becker–Han–Jitomirskaya–Zworski (honeycomb, arXiv:1803.00988).
results: The pendant-twin counterexample is correct. Attach two pendant vertices x,x' to each vertex of Z^2. Then delta_x - (phase) delta_x' is an eigenvector with eigenvalue 0 for every B. For E nonzero, E is in sigma iff E-2/E is in sigma(H_sq), which lies in [-4,4]. So a punctured neighbourhood of 0 is a gap, 0 is isolated, and the naive statement fails.
premise_risks: arXiv:2609.15812 (2026 preprint): 1D Robust Ten Martini; cited as a possible tool only, M does not depend on it.

plain: A tight-binding electron on any doubly periodic planar network in a uniform magnetic field: is the energy spectrum always a Cantor set when the flux per cell is irrational? This is known for the square lattice (Ten Martini), the honeycomb lattice and the Lieb lattice, each by a reduction to a one-dimensional operator. Flat-band eigenvalues that persist in any field can sit isolated, so they must be set aside. The question is whether what remains is always a Cantor set, or at least never contains an interval.
math: Let $G\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a connected planar graph with straight edges that is invariant under a lattice $L\cong\mathbb Z^2$ and has finitely many $L$-orbits of vertices. For a constant field $B$ with vector potential $A$, set $(H_B\psi)(x)=\sum_{y\sim x}e^{i\int_{[x,y]}A}\psi(y)$ on $\ell^2(V(G))$, and let $2\pi\alpha=B\cdot\mathrm{covol}(L)$. Let $\Sigma'$ be the derived set of $\sigma(H_B)$, i.e. $\sigma(H_B)$ minus its isolated points (eigenvalues of infinite multiplicity, i.e. flat bands). Prove or disprove: for every such $G$ and every irrational $\alpha$, $\Sigma'$ is a nonempty Cantor set. At minimum, decide whether $\sigma(H_B)$ is always nowhere dense. The first open instance is the kagome lattice in a uniform field. (The pure line-graph flux pattern, with no flux through the triangles, reduces to the honeycomb case.)
